summary: Adds a pagination helper. Slice arithmetic has an off-by-one bug that causes one extra item to leak into each page.

expected_findings.description: Off-by-one in slice end. 'end = start + per_page + 1' returns per_page+1 items instead of per_page. Should be 'end = start + per_page'. Python slices are exclusive on the upper bound, so items[start:start+per_page] returns exactly per_page items.

No validation of page or per_page. page=0 produces start=-per_page (negative slice, wraps to end of list); negative page produces wrong-direction slices; per_page=0 returns empty pages; very large per_page allows expensive requests. Should validate page >= 1 and 1 <= per_page <= some max.
Return type 'list' is unparameterized. Should be 'list[T]' or use a TypeVar to preserve the input element type.

should_not_flag: 1-indexing for pages — that's conventional for user-facing pagination and the docstring documents it.
Not returning a Pagination object with metadata (total, has_next, etc.) — fine for a simple helper, can be added by callers.
Slicing past the end of the list — Python handles this gracefully, no bug.
notes_for_arbiter: F1 is the most obvious bug in the corpus — a senior reviewer should catch it instantly. If the reviewer misses F1, the system has a serious recall problem. F2 is the kind of validation Devon habitually skips. F3 is a nit. Watch for false positives around 'magic number 20' — defaults are appropriate here, not magic.
